letters.summary: Conrad Alan Rockenhaus served Adrienne Rockenhaus a formal written demand to retract, correct, and cease publishing false and defamatory statements, preserving rights under Michigan law (MCL 600.2911(2)(b)) and the Texas Defamation Mitigation Act (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code Sec. 73.055). The letter documents that Conrad is alive — Redford Township Police confirmed a welfare check on June 24, 2026 — and demands retraction of false claims that he is dead, was murdered, or is a criminal imposter stealing VA benefits, including publications on conradrockenhausisdead.com, conradrockenhausisdead.cc, and associated social media accounts (@adezero, @JustCallMeJoeP, and others). It demands retraction of false statements in the Wayne County PPO petition, removal of stricken and denied federal filings from skyphusion.com, takedown of false-death websites, litigation-hold preservation of all related records, and warns that failure to comply will result in pursuit of all legal remedies including a federal civil action in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, Waco Division.

_seo_why: seo_name and seo_description exist because `heading` and `description` are
rendered in the page BODY, where naming the recipient is legitimate, AND
were fed to the JSON-LD block in _layouts/retraction.html, where under
Conrad's 2026-07-31 ruling they are not: indexable metadata names the CASE,
not PEOPLE. Same split as court / court_name in _data/courts.json.
The recipient is identified by ROLE here (the opposing party, a trustee)
rather than dropped, so the two letters still have distinct titles and a
reader can tell them apart without the metadata naming anybody.
